question: Should OpenClaw accept direct scanning of Codex rollout JSONL as the maintained fallback for native apply_patch failure diagnostics?
rationale: The implementation is bounded and tested, but it establishes a new dependency-internal filesystem and sensitive-data boundary that automated review cannot declare permanent without owner intent.

options.title: Accept after live canary
options.body: Approve the bounded rollout fallback after redacted runtime proof confirms correlation, latency, and diagnostic redaction on the bundled Codex version.

options.title: Require an upstream seam
options.body: Pause this PR and expose the failure detail through a supported Codex app-server field or event before integrating it into OpenClaw.

options.title: Keep projection-only errors
options.body: Close the PR and retain the existing higher-level failure diagnostic rather than owning rollout-file compatibility and redaction risk.

recommendation.title: Accept after live canary
recommendation.body: Approve the bounded rollout fallback after redacted runtime proof confirms correlation, latency, and diagnostic redaction on the bundled Codex version.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server runtime work makes this the strongest available owner signal for deciding whether this diagnostic boundary belongs in the harness.
